input.quote: (b) Licensee agrees to allow an independent Certified Public Accountant or other Audit Professional, (selected by mutual agreement) to audit and analyze appropriate accounting records to ensure compliance with all terms of this Agreement. Any such audit shall be permitted by Licensee within 30 days of Licensee's receipt of a written request of Licensor.
input.rationale: Article IV(b) binds Licensee (our party) to permit Licensor-initiated audits of its records with no cap on frequency, no advance notice period (the 30 days is a deadline for us to submit to the audit, not notice to us), no business-hours or minimal-interference limit, no confidentiality undertaking from the auditor, and no restriction confining access to accounting records rather than our systems. Unlimited, on-demand audits sit at the playbook walk-away line. Cost allocation is already compliant (p0064: Licensor bears cost unless a discrepancy exceeding 5% is found), and auditor independence/mutual selection is acceptable, so the minimal edit adds only the frequency, notice, business-hours, confidentiality and no-system-access limits to the second sentence of p0073.

proposal.summary: Add frequency, notice, business-hours, auditor confidentiality and no-system-access limits to the Licensee audit right
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have added the standard limits to the audit right — once per twelve months, 30 days' prior written notice, normal business hours, auditor under confidentiality, and records-only access with no access to our systems — since as drafted the audit is unlimited in frequency and effectively on demand. Cost allocation in the preceding paragraph (Licensor's cost absent a 5% discrepancy) is acceptable; we can accept 15 days' notice if 30 is impractical.

ops.oldText: Any such audit shall be permitted by Licensee within 30 days of Licensee's receipt of a written request of Licensor.
ops.newText: Any such audit shall be conducted no more than once in any twelve (12) month period, upon not less than thirty (30) days' prior written notice from Licensor, during Licensee's normal business hours and in a manner that does not unreasonably interfere with Licensee's business. Prior to any audit, the auditor shall execute a confidentiality undertaking in favor of Licensee, and shall be given access solely to the relevant accounting records (which Licensee may provide off-site or in electronic form); neither Licensor nor the auditor shall have any direct or remote access to Licensee's systems, networks or data.
